submissions.findingTextShort: FDA states that nicotine is the addictive substance in tobacco products.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Current FDA public-health guidance identifies nicotine as the addictive substance in tobacco products. A generic nicotine owner therefore cannot be represented as a routine low-risk wellness ingredient simply because some nicotine-containing medicines have approved cessation uses.
submissions.usageContext: Nicotine addiction and consumer-product safety governance
submissions.safetyContext: Addiction liability is intrinsic to generic nicotine framing and should not be erased by NRT evidence.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Risk differs by product, route, dose and user context; this finding does not equate all nicotine products with combustible tobacco risk.

submissions.findingTextShort: FDA-approved nicotine replacement therapies are safe and effective smoking-cessation products when used properly.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: FDA describes approved nicotine replacement therapies such as patches, gum and lozenges as safe and effective products designed to help adults quit smoking by reducing cravings and withdrawal symptoms. This evidence belongs to labeled NRT products and smoking-cessation use, not to generic nicotine, e-cigarettes, pouches, research products, or wellness supplementation.
submissions.populationContext: Adults using FDA-approved nicotine replacement therapy for smoking cessation
submissions.usageContext: Approved NRT product and cessation indication
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Product-specific regulatory evidence must not be transferred to non-NRT nicotine products or unrelated consumer goals.

submissions.findingTextShort: Generic nicotine and FDA-approved NRT require separate product/use evidence owners before recommendation or monetization logic can be trusted.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Nicotine is the active substance across multiple product classes with very different routes, toxicant profiles and regulatory purposes. FDA-approved NRT cessation evidence must remain attached to the specific NRT product/use context, while generic nicotine retains addiction and product-specific safety uncertainty. Resolver and recommendation logic should therefore fail closed on cross-product evidence inheritance.
submissions.populationContext: Nicotine users across therapeutic and non-therapeutic product contexts
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This is a product-identity constraint; it does not assign one identical risk profile to every nicotine delivery system.
